Weave & Base Fabric.name: Katan Silk Banarasi
Weave & Base Fabric.description: Woven from pure twisted mulberry silk yarn (katan), this is considered the purest and most traditional Banarasi base — crisp, lustrous, and the foundation on which most classic zari work is done.
Weave & Base Fabric.notes: Considered the gold standard base fabric for authentic handloom Banarasi sarees.

Weave & Base Fabric.name: Organza (Kora) Banarasi
Weave & Base Fabric.occasion: Summer wedding functions, daytime festive wear
Weave & Base Fabric.description: Woven with a sheer, lightweight silk-and-zari base that gives a translucent, airy drape, making it far cooler to wear than dense katan silk while retaining the zari motifs.
Weave & Base Fabric.notes: A popular choice for summer weddings and daytime functions where heavier silk feels impractical.

Weave & Base Fabric.name: Georgette Banarasi
Weave & Base Fabric.description: Uses a georgette base instead of pure silk, giving a softer fall and fluid drape while still carrying traditional Banarasi motifs — a lighter, more contemporary alternative.
Weave & Base Fabric.materials: Georgette, zari and silk thread motifs
Weave & Base Fabric.notes: Favoured for its softer drape and lower weight compared to katan silk versions.

Weave & Base Fabric.name: Shattir (Mixed Silk) Banarasi
Weave & Base Fabric.description: Woven using a mix of silk and cotton or art-silk yarns, producing a more affordable, slightly stiffer fabric that still carries the characteristic Banarasi brocade patterning.
Weave & Base Fabric.materials: Mixed silk-cotton or art-silk yarn, zari
Weave & Base Fabric.notes: A budget-friendly entry point into Banarasi weaving, common in mass retail.

Weaving Technique.name: Jangla Banarasi
Weaving Technique.description: One of the oldest Banarasi weaving styles, featuring dense, all-over intricate patterns of flora and vines covering nearly the entire body of the saree in a jungle-like (jangla) spread.
Weaving Technique.materials: Silk, dense zari vine and floral motifs
Weaving Technique.notes: One of the most labour-intensive traditional Banarasi weaves, taking weeks to months on the loom.

Weaving Technique.name: Tanchoi Banarasi
Weaving Technique.description: Uses an extra-weft satin weaving technique originally brought from China via Surat, producing a smooth, closely-woven fabric with small, delicate motifs and minimal use of zari.
Weaving Technique.notes: Distinct for its subtle sheen and fine motifs rather than heavy gold work, giving it a more understated elegance.

Weaving Technique.name: Cutwork Banarasi
Weaving Technique.description: Motifs are woven with floating threads that are later cut away by hand, leaving crisp, clean patterns against a plain or lightly-worked background — giving a net-like, airy effect.
Weaving Technique.materials: Silk or silk-cotton blend, cutwork motifs
Weaving Technique.notes: Lighter and more affordable than dense zari weaves, popular for everyday festive wear.

Weaving Technique.name: Butidar Banarasi
Weaving Technique.description: Small individual motifs (butis) are scattered evenly across the body of the saree, each woven separately, giving a refined, all-over sprinkled pattern rather than a continuous design.
Weaving Technique.notes: The scattered-motif technique is one of the most recognisable classic Banarasi styles.

Zari & Brocade Style.name: Kimkhwab (Pure Zari) Banarasi
Zari & Brocade Style.description: The most opulent Banarasi variety, woven with real gold and silver zari in a dense brocade so heavy it was historically called 'kimkhwab' — meaning 'little dream' — for its rarity and richness.
Zari & Brocade Style.materials: Pure silk, real gold/silver zari brocade
Zari & Brocade Style.notes: Historically reserved for royalty; among the most expensive Banarasi sarees produced today.

Zari & Brocade Style.name: Meenakari Banarasi
Zari & Brocade Style.description: Coloured enamel-like threads (meenakari) are woven alongside gold or silver zari to create a two-tone shimmer effect within the motifs, echoing the meenakari enamelling craft of jewellery.
Zari & Brocade Style.materials: Silk, zari with coloured meenakari thread accents
Zari & Brocade Style.notes: The colour-shift effect within the gold motifs is the defining visual signature of this style.

Zari & Brocade Style.name: Tissue Banarasi
Zari & Brocade Style.description: Fine gold or silver zari threads are woven directly into the body of the fabric rather than confined to motifs, giving the entire saree a shimmering, metallic sheen.
Zari & Brocade Style.materials: Silk with zari woven through the body
Zari & Brocade Style.notes: The shimmer changes appearance under different lighting, similar to tissue Kanjeevaram sarees.

Zari & Brocade Style.name: Rangkat Banarasi
Zari & Brocade Style.description: Two or more colours are used within the same weave using the ikat-influenced 'rangkat' technique, creating a subtle colour-blend effect across the body of the saree.
Zari & Brocade Style.notes: Prized for its subtle, gradient-like colour transitions rather than sharp contrast blocks.

Border & Pallu Style.name: Shikargah Banarasi
Border & Pallu Style.description: Depicts hunting scenes (shikar) with animals, birds, and foliage woven across the pallu in intricate narrative detail, drawing directly on Mughal court textile traditions.
Border & Pallu Style.materials: Silk, dense narrative zari pallu work
Border & Pallu Style.notes: One of the rarest and most historically significant Banarasi motifs, seldom mass-produced.

Border & Pallu Style.name: Temple Border Banarasi
Border & Pallu Style.description: Features a stepped, zigzag temple-tower border similar to South Indian temple-border sarees, blending a South Indian motif tradition with North Indian Banarasi weaving.
Border & Pallu Style.notes: A cross-regional fusion style popular with buyers who want temple-border aesthetics on a Banarasi weave.

Border & Pallu Style.name: Paisley (Kalga-Bel) Banarasi
Border & Pallu Style.description: The border and pallu carry a continuous vine (bel) interspersed with paisley (kalga) motifs, one of the most classic and widely recognised Banarasi border patterns.
Border & Pallu Style.notes: Among the most commonly seen Banarasi border designs across price points.
